name: hrc
help:
Usage: hrc [--agent|--human] <command> [options]

VIEW: agent
  Override with --human. The complete maintenance cellar is always visible via:
  hrc admin --help

AGENT COMMANDS
  server status        show daemon/socket/API health state
  session list         list sessions
  monitor show         show the current monitor-state snapshot and counters, unlike hrc ls or hrc runtime list inventory
  monitor wait         watch --until without the event stream, using the same condition engine
  monitor watch        stream monitor events
  monitor search       search completed transcript turns across runtimes with the resident BM25 index
  monitor events       list durable invocation-ledger events (invocation-local seq; never used by monitor conditions)
  monitor transcript   render an invocation activity transcript (tool starts/results, completed assistant messages, driver notices)
  monitor stats        summarize durable invocation-ledger activity
  start                start a managed runtime
  run                  launch or reattach and attach
  resume               resume the latest stored continuation for a target (regardless of status)
  show                 show a runtime, host session, or message by selector
  ls                   list runtimes | sessions | messages
  turn                 dispatch tracked work or attach to an admitted turn and stream its progress
  summon               materialize/pre-warm a target; message traffic auto-summons when needed
  restart              end a scope's conversation and relaunch it fresh (generation+1, no continuation); refuses a busy seat
  restartme            restart this agent into a fresh context when the current turn ends (needs a pending wrkq handoff)
  send                 inject literal input into a live tmux runtime; no envelope or obligation; not for tracked work
  peek                 tail the live tmux pane of a bound runtime
  attach               attach to a live runtime
  runtime list         list runtimes (use `hrc show <scope>` or `runtime inspect <id>` for one target)
  runtime inspect      inspect nested HRC and broker authority views for a runtime
  runtime diagnostics  list first_turn_missing trips, or print one trip and its diagnostic bundle (read-only)
  runtime terminate    terminate a runtime
  target locate        show declared policy, established binding, and observed runtimes for a scope
  doctor               check daemon health, node identity, placement skew, and one target

Run hrc <command> --help for the complete help of any explicitly named command.
humanHelp:
Usage: hrc [--agent|--human] <command> [options]

VIEW: human
  Override with --agent. The complete maintenance cellar is always visible via:
  hrc admin --help

GROUPS
  server      daemon lifecycle, health, and tmux backend control
  session     resolve, list, and inspect sessions
  monitor     show, watch, and wait on HRC monitor state
  admin       administrative maintenance commands
  capture     inspect or release broker capture state
  runtime     list, inspect, and control runtimes
  federation  inspect and operate federation
  target      inspect where scopes live (placement)

HUMAN FLOWS
  hrc run <target>
    launch or reattach and attach
  hrc attach <target>
    attach to a live runtime

OTHER COMMANDS
  info    show HRC orientation and first-contact guidance
  doctor  check daemon health, node identity, placement skew, and one target

Run hrc <command> --help for the complete help of any explicitly named command.

children.name: stop
children.help:
Usage: hrc server stop [options]

ask the HRC daemon to stop itself (authorized server-side)

Options:
  --reason <text>         why (required)
  --node <nodeId>         stop a peer node daemon over federation (mable primary
                          only)
  --force                 skip the in-flight check
  --wait                  wait for in-flight runs to drain before stopping
  --wait-timeout-ms <n>   max time to wait for in-flight drain (default 300000)
  --proof-timeout-ms <n>  max time to observe the daemon gone (default 30000)
  -h, --help              display help for command

Authorization (T-09861): the daemon decides, never this CLI or its env.
  Allowed: mable@<project>:primary on any node (--node <id> for a peer node),
           and on its own node only mable@<project>:minisvc (svc) or
           mable@hrc-runtime:hrcdev (hrcdev). Everyone else is refused.
  --reason <text> is required. A daemon that predates the contract is refused
  with the documented break-glass: launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.praesidium.hrc-server
  This stops accidental and doctrinal violations and records deliberate ones;
  it does not stop a determined same-uid actor.

children.name: wait
children.help:
Usage: hrc monitor wait [options] [selectors...]

watch --until without the event stream, using the same condition engine

Arguments:
  selectors                 one or more exact, scope-prefix, or task-id
                            selectors

Options:
  --until <condition>       exact selector condition (repeat for OR):
                            turn-finished, idle, busy, response, runtime-dead
                            (default: [])
  --until-any <condition>   set condition; first matching member wins (repeat
                            for OR): turn-finished, idle, busy, response,
                            runtime-dead (default: [])
  --until-all <condition>   set condition; every frozen member must match
                            (repeat for OR; levels only) (default: [])
  --timeout <duration>      maximum wait duration
  --stall-after <duration>  stall threshold duration
  --since <seq|duration>    terminal evidence fence; exact cursors are safest
                            for scripts, durations are a human convenience
  --json                    output structured JSON
  -h, --help                display help for command

Task, prefix, and multiple-selector waits require --until-any or --until-all. --until-all accepts levels only and freezes membership at arm.
Exit codes: 0 matched after arm/replay (outcome=success); 10 already true at arm (outcome=success); 2 usage (no terminal event); 11 no session ever (outcome=not_matched); 12 runtime-death obstruction (outcome=not_matched); 13 observed terminal failure (outcome=observed_failure); 20 timeout (outcome=not_matched); 21 stall (outcome=not_matched); 22 context change (outcome=not_matched); 23 monitor error (outcome=error); 130 SIGINT (outcome=error).

Usage: hrc resume <scope> [options]

  Resume the most recent stored continuation for a target, REGARDLESS of its
  HRC status (archived / dormant / broken / removed-orphaned). Unlike `hrc run`,
  resume NEVER starts a fresh session and NEVER attaches as a substitute for
  resume — it requires a captured provider continuation and fails clearly if
  none was ever recorded. Explicit clear/drop/end operations do not erase or
  invalidate the stored provider continuation.

  <scope>  Agent scope: agent, agent@project, or full scope ref.
           When run from a project directory, the project is inferred
           automatically (e.g. "larry" becomes "larry@agent-spaces").

Options:
  --no-attach          Resume and start without attaching to the tmux session
  --prior              Resume the current session's immediate predecessor
  --host-session <id>  Resume an exact historical host session
  --dry-run            Local plan preview — no side effects
  --debug              Keep tmux shell alive after harness exits
  --project-id <id>    Override the inferred project id (cwd is treated as its root)
  --project-root <dir> Override project root (defaults to cwd when --project-id is set)
  --cwd <path>         Set execution cwd without changing the resolved project root

Options:
  --no-attach            resume and start without attaching to the tmux session
  --prior                resume the current session's immediate predecessor
  --host-session <id>    resume an exact historical host session
  --dry-run              local plan preview — no side effects

Semantics:

  default, the active session's predecessor with --prior, or an exact historical

  --no-attach            resume and start without attaching to the tmux session
  --prior                resume the current session's immediate predecessor
  --host-session <id>    resume an exact historical host session
  --dry-run              local plan preview — no side effects
  --debug                keep tmux shell alive after harness exits
  --no-register          do not prompt to register cwd as a project marker
  --json                 on error, emit structured JSON (includes broker
                         rejection detail)
  --project-id <id>      override the inferred project id
  --project-root <path>  override project root
  --cwd <path>           set execution cwd without changing the resolved project
                         root
  -p <text>              initial prompt to send to the harness
  --prompt-file <path>   read initial prompt from a file
  -h, --help             display help for command

Semantics:
  resume force-resumes the selected stored continuation for a target: newest by
  default, the active session's predecessor with --prior, or an exact historical
  row with --host-session. Selection is REGARDLESS of HRC status (archived /
  dormant / broken / removed-orphaned).
  Unlike `hrc run`, it requires a captured continuation: if none has ever been
  recorded, it fails clearly and does NOT start fresh. Clear/drop/terminate audit
  events never erase or invalidate a recorded continuation for explicit resume.
  For attach-only behavior use `hrc attach <scope>`; for start/reuse/attach use
  `hrc run <scope>`.

Usage: hrc target locate [options] <scope>

show declared policy, established binding, and observed runtimes for a scope

Arguments:
  scope           scope ref or target handle (e.g. clod@hrc-runtime:T-06613)

Options:
  --json          output as JSON
  --fail-on-skew  exit 1 when placement disagrees with the established binding
  -h, --help      display help for command

Reports three independent truths, so a disagreement between them stays visible:
  declared  what the agent profile [placement] stanza says
  authority the established binding (local ledger first, then the registry)
  observed  runtimes running on THIS node (peer observation is F1)

SKEW is an exact pin or matched task-default disagreeing with an established
binding. The established home keeps summon authority and the policy edit is
not acted on — editing placement does not relocate a scope that already exists.

An ordinary explicit start away from default_home_node is expected, not skew.
External registrations are mechanism-born: their default_home_node remains governing policy.

Exit codes:
  0  reported (including when skew is present)
  1  skew present and --fail-on-skew was passed
  2  usage error

hrc — HRC agent runbook

VIEW: agent
  Override with --human. The complete maintenance cellar is always visible via:
  hrc admin --help

SELECTORS
  runtime:<id> | host:<id> | session:<ref> | scope:<ref> | msg:<id> | seq:<n> | <target-handle>
  Raw native IDs win first; explicit prefixes win by type; ambiguous bare selectors fail closed.

OUTPUT
  JSON is one complete document. NDJSON is one complete object per line.
  Never parse terminal-oriented human/tree output in automation.

SERVER STATUS JSON
  hrc server status --json is one document, and every path below is also printed by the
  human render. Nothing is emitted at the top level under a shorter name — jq answers
  null for a path that does not exist, so a typo reads exactly like a dead daemon.
    node.nodeId                     this node's id (NOT .nodeId)
    release.mode                    "atomic" | "unmanaged" — assert this first
    release.releaseId               installed atomic release (NOT .release.id)
    release.hrcBuild.sourceCommit   running HRC commit (NOT .sourceCommit)
    release.hrcBuild.setVersion     running HRC set version (NOT .hrcBuild.version)
    release.processStartedAt        when the running process started (NOT .processStartedAt)
    release.runningEqualsInstalled  true when running == installed release
    schema.schemaAhead              true in the install→restart window: the store lacks migrations this release carries
  Assert release.mode == "atomic" before reading any other release.* path, and read with
  jq -e: it exits nonzero on a path that does not exist, where jq -r prints a bare null
  no different from a real one. That is the whole failure this contract exists to end.

CURSORS
  monitor show/watch/wait use global hrcSeq replay and condition fences.
  monitor events/transcript/stats use invocation-local broker seq. The grammars are distinct.
  Monitor conditions NEVER evaluate the broker invocation ledger.

PLACEMENT
  hrc start/resume --cwd <absolute-path> changes execution cwd without changing project root.

SELF-RESTART
  To restart into fresh context: write a handoff, `hrc restartme --handoff <id>`, end your turn.

RUNBOOK
  hrc server status
    show daemon/socket/API health state
    Example: hrc server status --json
    Exit:    0 healthy; 1 not running; 2 degraded/usage; 3 probe failure
    Output:  --json emits one status document, named paths under SERVER STATUS JSON in hrc info --agent

  hrc session list
    list sessions
    Example: hrc session list --scope cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 --json
    Exit:    0 success; 2 usage; 1 read failure
    Output:  --json is one array; --porcelain is stable tab-separated output

  hrc monitor show
    show the current monitor-state snapshot and counters, unlike hrc ls or hrc runtime list inventory
    Example: hrc monitor show T-07011 --json
    Exit:    0 snapshot read; 2 usage; 23 daemon/read failure
    Output:  --json is one snapshot document keyed by global hrcSeq

  hrc monitor wait
    watch --until without the event stream, using the same condition engine
    Example: hrc monitor wait T-07011 --until-all runtime-dead --timeout 5m --json
    Exit:    0 matched (success); 10 already true at arm (success); 2 usage/no event; 11 no session ever (not_matched); 12 runtime death obstruction (not_matched); 13 terminal failure (observed_failure); 20 timeout (not_matched); 21 stall (not_matched); 22 context change (not_matched); 23 monitor error (error); 130 SIGINT (error)
    Output:  --json emits one condition result; timeout is semantic exit 20, not command failure

  hrc monitor watch
    stream monitor events
    Example: hrc monitor watch T-07011 --follow --format ndjson
    Exit:    0 matched (success); 10 already true at arm (success); 2 usage/no event; 11 no session ever (not_matched); 12 runtime death obstruction (not_matched); 13 terminal failure (observed_failure); 20 timeout (not_matched); 21 stall (not_matched); 22 context change (not_matched); 23 monitor error (error); 130 SIGINT (error)
    Output:  non-TTY defaults to NDJSON; each line is one complete normalized HRC event

  hrc monitor search
    search completed transcript turns across runtimes with the resident BM25 index
    Example: hrc monitor search "deployment failed" --project hrc-runtime --json
    Exit:    0 success; 2 query/usage error; 1 read failure
    Output:  ranked turn pointers plus resident-index lag

  hrc monitor events
    list durable invocation-ledger events (invocation-local seq; never used by monitor conditions)
    Example: hrc monitor events runtime:<id> --latest --ndjson
    Exit:    0 success; 2 usage; 1 read failure
    Output:  --ndjson is one broker event per line; --seq is invocation-local

  hrc monitor transcript
    render an invocation activity transcript (tool starts/results, completed assistant messages, driver notices)
    Example: hrc monitor transcript cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 --previous --tail 100
    Exit:    0 success; 2 usage; 1 read failure
    Output:  invocation activity, not conversation readback; events --ndjson is structured

  hrc monitor stats
    summarize durable invocation-ledger activity
    Example: hrc monitor stats runtime:<id> --latest --json
    Exit:    0 success; 2 usage; 1 read failure
    Output:  --json emits one invocation-ledger summary

  hrc start
    start a managed runtime
    Example: hrc start cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 -p "Continue."
    Exit:    0 provisioned; 2 usage; 1 launch failure
    Output:  detached provision result; --json structures errors

  hrc run
    launch or reattach and attach
    Example: hrc run cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011
    Exit:    0 attached session ended normally; 2 usage; 1 launch/attach failure
    Output:  interactive TTY flow; use start for detached automation

  hrc resume
    resume the latest stored continuation for a target (regardless of status)
    Example: hrc resume cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011
    Exit:    0 continuation resumed; 2 usage; 1 invalidated/missing continuation or launch failure
    Output:  continuation-only recovery; never fresh-launches and refuses --force-restart

  hrc show
    show a runtime, host session, or message by selector
    Example: hrc show scope:agent:cody:project:hrc-runtime:task:T-07011 --json
    Exit:    0 resolved; 2 usage/ambiguity; 1 read failure
    Output:  --json names the resolved kind plus concrete IDs

  hrc ls
    list runtimes | sessions | messages
    Example: hrc ls runtimes --status busy --json
    Exit:    0 success; 2 invalid noun/flags; 1 read failure
    Output:  noun-specific structured output; narrow large runtime lists with filters

  hrc turn
    dispatch tracked work or attach to an admitted turn and stream its progress
    Example: hrc turn cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 "Continue."
    Exit:    the dispatched turn exit code
    Output:  streams the turn output verbatim

  hrc summon
    materialize/pre-warm a target; message traffic auto-summons when needed
    Example: hrc summon cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011
    Exit:    0 target materialized or already live; 2 usage; 1 summon refused or failed
    Output:  sessionRef, state, generation, and the dm/send/peek capability triple

  hrc restart
    end a scope's conversation and relaunch it fresh (generation+1, no continuation); refuses a busy seat
    Example: hrc restart clod@hrc-ios:T-10850
    Exit:    0 restarted and launched; 1 refused (busy, unobservable, stale, not restartable) or launch failed; 2 usage
    Output:  old → new generation and the launched runtime; a refusal changes nothing; a failed launch prints the hrc start recovery

  hrc restartme
    restart this agent into a fresh context when the current turn ends (needs a pending wrkq handoff)
    Example: hrc restartme --handoff H-00123
    Exit:    0 armed or cancelled; 1 refused (no handoff, wrong-scope or non-pending handoff, no credential, no active turn); 2 usage
    Output:  write a handoff (wrkq handoff create --scope <agent>@<project>), arm, then END YOUR TURN; the successor (generation+1, fresh context) starts by consuming the handoff

  hrc send
    inject literal input into a live tmux runtime; no envelope or obligation; not for tracked work
    Example: hrc send cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 "y"
    Exit:    0 delivered; 2 usage; 1 no live runtime to inject into
    Output:  raw keystrokes into a live pane; returns a runId and lands in hrc_events, but no wrkc envelope or obligation — use `wrkc say` for tracked work

  hrc peek
    tail the live tmux pane of a bound runtime
    Example: hrc peek cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 --lines 40
    Exit:    0 captured; 2 usage; 1 no bound runtime
    Output:  the pane text as captured; --json wraps it with capture metadata

  hrc attach
    attach to a live runtime
    Example: hrc attach cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 --dry-run
    Exit:    0 attached or plan emitted; 2 usage; 1 when no live runtime exists
    Output:  --dry-run emits the attach plan without launching or mutating

  hrc runtime list
    list runtimes (use `hrc show <scope>` or `runtime inspect <id>` for one target)
    Example: hrc runtime list --status busy --task T-07011 --json
    Exit:    0 success; 2 usage; 1 read/federation failure
    Output:  one JSON array locally; --all-nodes returns a node-labeled projection

  hrc runtime inspect
    inspect nested HRC and broker authority views for a runtime
    Example: hrc runtime inspect runtime:<id> --json
    Exit:    0 success; 2 selector/usage error; 1 read/probe failure
    Output:  --json preserves separate hrc and broker authority objects

  hrc runtime diagnostics
    list first_turn_missing trips, or print one trip and its diagnostic bundle (read-only)
    Example: hrc runtime diagnostics 41822 --json
    Exit:    0 success; 2 usage; 1 read failure or unknown trip
    Output:  trips list, or one trip plus its redacted bundle manifest

  hrc runtime terminate
    terminate a runtime
    Example: hrc runtime terminate runtime:<id> --no-drop-continuation
    Exit:    0 terminated; 2 usage/conflicting flags; 1 termination failure
    Output:  JSON mutation result (with or without --json); choose continuation preservation explicitly

  hrc target locate
    show declared policy, established binding, and observed runtimes for a scope
    Example: hrc target locate cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 --json --fail-on-skew
    Exit:    0 reported; 1 placement skew with --fail-on-skew; 2 usage/read failure
    Output:  --json keeps declared, authority, and observed placement truths distinct

  hrc doctor
    check daemon health, node identity, placement skew, and one target
    Example: hrc doctor cody@hrc-runtime:T-07011 --json
    Exit:    0 healthy; 1 failing check or warning under --strict; 2 usage
    Output:  --json emits one check report; a <target> adds its reachability checks to the same report

info.human:
hrc — HRC operator guide

VIEW: human
  Override with --agent. The complete maintenance cellar is always visible via:
  hrc admin --help

ABOUT
  HRC is the local runtime control plane for agent targets, continuity sessions, and live runtimes.
  Use hrc to inspect or control runtime state (execution); use wrkc to talk to agents
  (collaboration). Only 'wrkc say --to' fires — a say without it is a room log entry.

GROUPS
  server      daemon lifecycle, health, and tmux backend control
  session     resolve, list, and inspect sessions
  monitor     show, watch, and wait on HRC monitor state
  admin       administrative maintenance commands
  capture     inspect or release broker capture state
  runtime     list, inspect, and control runtimes
  federation  inspect and operate federation
  target      inspect where scopes live (placement)

HUMAN FLOWS
  hrc run <target>
    launch or reattach and attach
  hrc attach <target>
    attach to a live runtime

OTHER COMMANDS
  info    show HRC orientation and first-contact guidance
  doctor  check daemon health, node identity, placement skew, and one target

MODEL
  target = who you mean; session = continuity; runtime = the live execution.
  Start/reuse/attach with hrc run. Attach without launching with hrc attach.
  Resume is continuation-only recovery: it never fresh-launches and is not an alias of run.
  hrc start/resume --cwd <absolute-path> changes execution cwd without changing project root.
